description.text: Set the consistency between the left and right disparity vectors. Increase consistency to encourage the vectors to match.

Restrict occlusions to regions where disparity is not consistent. Occlusions are detected where the discrepancy between left and right disparity is greater than the consistency threshold. Reduce the threshold to mark more areas as occlusions.
Dilate occlusions into the background region. Increase dilation to ensure that no occluded pixels are used when rebuilding views with disparity.

This is the GPU that will be used for rendering, when Use GPU if available is selected. If you have more than one GPU in your machine, you can select a different GPU Device to use by editing your Preferences. (Note that selecting a different GPU will require a restart of Nuke to take effect.) Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. Please refer to the documentation for details of the requirements for GPU acceleration. * It was not possible to create a context for processing on the selected GPU. For example, this can happen when there is not enough free memory available on the GPU. To use the GPU when rendering from the command line, add --gpu to your command.
Mark occlusions at depth changes. Occlusions are detected where the change in disparity exceeds the gradient threshold. Reduce the threshold to mark more areas as occlusions.

Select the input projection.
Choose 'Latlong'' to impose spherical continuity in the vector calculation.
Set the left view to use.
Set a mask defining the valid image region for matching.
Set the number of iterations in the vector calculation. Increase for more accurate vectors, but with a longer computation time.
Set the right view to use.

Set disparity smoothness to control depth changes at image edges. In high contrast images, increase the smoothness to reduce depth separation at image edges. In low contrast images, decrease the smoothness to pick up depth changes on image edges.
Set the strength in matching images. Increase to force image alignment, decrease to make the vectors smoother.

Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. The GPU will then be used whenever the script is opened on a machine which does have a GPU available. You should also select this if you wish to render from the command line with the --gpu option. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.
Controls the density of the disparity vectors. Increase for higher resolution vectors, but also longer computation time.

Choose the output space of the disparity vectors.
Default (wrapped) - The vectors will always sample pixels inside the image bounds.
Continuous - The vectors will be continuous but will not always sample within the image bounds. Use this option if you want to apply any standard filtering operation (such as rescaling) to the disparity vectors.
Set the number of warps in the vector calculation. Increase to handle large image displacements, but with a longer computation time.

description.text:
C_DisparityGenerator 2.1v5: Calculate the disparity vectors between a left, right image pair.

Input: Set the left and right views, and choose a 'Latlong' projection to calculate disparity with spherical continuity.

Vector Generation: Control the detail and matching in the disparity calculation.

Disparity defines the connection between left and right images. The disparityL channel defines the match in the left image at each pixel in the right and disparityR matches the right image at each pixel in the left.

Note: Disparity will only be computed within the format bounds.
